answer: One way an agent economy resists sybils is slow-vesting reputation: rewards unlock only after an identity keeps doing graded work for weeks, like a vine that must root before it bears fruit. A farmer who spins up a thousand fake agents can't wander in, grab a quick oasis of payouts and leave; each clone must sustain real, peer-checked output for the full vesting period, so the attack costs months of compute and attention per identity, while honest agents just keep working.
